 Stock Radar: BSE stock up over 10% in a month, technical charts hint at a bottom?
 SECTIONS Stock Radar: BSE stock up over 10% in a month, technical charts hint at a bottom? By Kshitij Anand , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 11, 2026, 05:00:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis BSE Ltd has recently broken out from an inverse head and shoulder pattern, indicating potential upward movement. The stock has previously experienced a correction but found support around Rs 3,000 levels. Experts predict a target above Rs 4,000 in the coming months if the stock sustains above crucial support levels. The daily MACD indicates bullish momentum, while the RSI shows it may still have room for growth.
 Agencies BSE stock has broken out of an inverse head & shoulder pattern which, experts say is a sign for more growth in the next few months.
 BSE Ltd , part of the financial services industry, broke out from the neckline of an inverse head & shoulder pattern which has opened room for the stock to head higher.
 Medium-term traders can look to buy the stock for a target above 4,000 levels in the next few months, suggest experts.
The stock hit a high of Rs 4,446 on 25th May 2026, but it failed to hold the momentum. It closed at Rs 3,800 on November 6, 2026 which translates into a fall of 15%.
The stock seems to have formed a bottom around 3,000 levels in September & October. It has rallied more than 8% in a week and over 13% in a month, data showed.
The recent spike also pushed the stock above the neckline of an inverse head & shoulder pattern which is a bullish sign.
 Live Events
 The stock may be trading in the overbought zone, but as long as it holds above crucial support levels, any decline could present a good buying opportunity.
 An Inverse Head & Shoulders is a bullish reversal pattern typically appears after a downtrend and suggests that selling pressure may be weakening, with the potential for an upward reversal. A breakout from the neckline suggests a shift in momentum from sellers to buyers.
 The daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) is placed at 70.1. RSI above 70 is considered overbought. This implies that stock may show pullback.
The daily MACD is above its center and signal Line, this is a bullish indicator.
 ETMarkets.com BSE Ltd. has been witnessing a strong primary uptrend on the weekly chart since August 2023, culminating in an all-time high of Rs 4,446 in May 2026.
“BSE stock underwent a healthy correction of approximately 32%, finding strong support near the Rs 3,000 mark, which acted as a Change in Polarity (CIP) zone. Following this corrective phase, the stock has once again resumed its primary uptrend, indicating renewed buying interest,” Vidnyan S. Sawant, Head of Research, GEPL Capital, said.
“On the daily chart, the stock has delivered a breakout from an Inverted Head & Shoulders pattern, a bullish reversal formation, signalling a potential continuation of the upward momentum,” he added.
Furthermore, the stock continues to maintain a Higher High–Higher Low formation across the daily, weekly and monthly timeframes, reinforcing the strength of its overall bullish structure.
Momentum indicators are also supporting the positive outlook. The MACD has generated a fresh bullish crossover above the zero line, accompanied by a rising histogram, indicating strengthening upward momentum.
Meanwhile, the RSI, currently at 60, has moved above its average and is trending higher, suggesting sustained buying strength with further room for upside.
“Going forward, the Rs 3,470–3,450 zone remains a crucial support area and breakout level. As long as the stock sustains above this zone, the bullish bias is likely to remain intact, with a potential upside target of Rs 4,250–4,300 in the short to medium term,” recommended Sawant.
“Immediate support is placed near Rs 3,450, coinciding with the 5-day EMA. However, a weekly closing below this level could signal a failed breakout and warrant caution,” he added.
“From a trading perspective, traders may maintain a positive bias and consider a closing-basis stop loss at Rs 3,450, while tracking Rs 4,250–4,300 as the next potential resistance and target zone,” highlighted Sawant.
